lede: Tuesday is the week's heaviest lift: a newly seated Town Council takes up second reading of the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code, which would lock wildfire-resilient landscaping and historic-review standards into the Land Use Code — a real vote with real consequences for property owners. That same day, the Telluride Housing Authority considers a new primary-residency policy for dependents of multiple custodial parents, and Thursday's Planning & Zoning session digs into subdivision and concept-plan applications for the Town-owned Carhenge redevelopment on West Pacific.

notable.stake: Second reading vote on wildfire code changes to Land Use Code landscaping and historic review.
New primary-residency policy for dependents of split-custody households could affect deed-restricted eligibility.
Town-owned Carhenge site faces subdivision and concept-plan hearings — public land use decision.
